job.title: Project Architect
job.description:
Senior Project Architect 


I'm currently partnering with a nationally recognised architecture studio that has built an outstanding reputation for delivering high-quality developments across Australia. Due to a strong pipeline of projects and continued growth, they are looking to appoint an experienced Senior Project Architect to play a key role in leading multi-residential projects from design development through to completion.

Looking for Brisbane architects who enjoy being involved throughout the project lifecycle — from early concept and design development through to documentation, approvals, tender and construction. 

As a Senior Project Architect, you'll take ownership of major multi-residential projects, ensuring exceptional design outcomes are delivered on time and within budget. You'll work closely with clients, consultants, and internal teams throughout every stage of the project lifecycle.

Key Responsibilities:
  • Lead the delivery of multi-residential projects from early stages, through to construction.
  • Engage directly with clients and consultants building strong and collaborative connections. 
  • Develop project briefs, scopes of work and design strategies.
  • Lead concept design and design development, working independently as well as collaboratively within a team.
  • Resolve design and technical challenges throughout project delivery.
  • Maintain high design standards while ensuring commercial project outcomes.
  • Contribute to a collaborative studio environment, providing mentorship to junior graduates, bringing a proactive and creative approach to projects.
What we look for:
  • Registered Architect or working towards registration.
  • 8+ years' experience within an Australian architectural practice.
  • Strong background delivering multi-residential apartment projects.
  • Excellent Revit documentation skills.
  • Sound understanding of the NCC, Australian Standards, and local planning requirements.
  • Proven experience coordinating consultants and managing project delivery.
  • Strong communication and client-facing skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
If you're looking to take the next step in your architectural career and join a practice with an outstanding reputation and an exciting future, I'd love to have a confidential conversation.

Click "Apply Now" or contact Brittany Steinbach on bsteinbach@designandbuild.com.au with an updated resume and portfolio. Your application will be treated as strictly confidential.

job.title: Site Manager - Long term opportunity on high profile project
job.description:
Site Manager | $300m Defence Project | Adelaide Major Defence Infrastructure Project | Long Term Career Opportunity | Tier 1 Builder
  • Deliver a signifcant package on a landmark $300m defence training facility. 
  • Join a leading national Tier 1 builder with a strong pipeline of varied projects
  • Permanent opportunity with paid Saturday work and long term project security
The Opportunity

Design & Build Recruitment is partnering with one of Australia's leading Tier 1 construction companies to appoint an experienced Site Manager for a major $300m defence infrastructure project.

The project involves the delivery of a large scale, training facility, incorporating complex structural elements, extensive façade packages to house high quality educational facilities.

This is an excellent opportunity to join a well established project team delivering critical infrastructure that will play an important role in supporting Australia's defence capability for years to come.

The Role

Reporting to an experienced Senior Site Manager, you will work alongside four other Site Managers, taking responsibility for the successful delivery of significant façade and external building packages.

Your responsibilities will include:
  • Managing the day to day delivery of façade and associated construction works.
  • Coordinating subcontractors, trades, materials and site resources.
  • Driving programme, productivity and construction milestones.
  • Ensuring works are delivered to the highest standards of safety, quality and compliance.
  • Managing subcontractor performance and resolving technical and construction challenges.
  • Working closely with the Senior Site Manager, engineering and project delivery teams.
  • Coordinating interfaces between structural, façade and other construction packages.
  • Maintaining strong communication with project stakeholders and contributing to a collaborative site culture.
About You We're looking for an experienced Site Manager who has developed their career delivering significant commercial, institutional or defence construction projects.

Ideally, you will demonstrate:
  • Proven experience as a Site Manager with a Tier 1 or Tier 2 commercial builder.
  • Strong experience delivering large scale structural and façade packages.
  • Previous exposure to defence projects or similarly complex, highly regulated construction environments.
  • Experience managing significant subcontractor packages on projects of substantial value.
  • Strong knowledge of construction sequencing, programming, safety and quality management.
  • Excellent communication skills and the ability to work effectively within a large project delivery team.
  • A practical, solutions focused approach and a strong commitment to successful project outcomes.
Defence security requirements: Applicants must be able to satisfy the project's nationality, background and security screening requirements. Specific eligibility criteria will be confirmed during the recruitment process.
What's on Offer?
  • Major Project: Contribute to the delivery of a landmark $300m defence training facility.
  • Career Security: Permanent employment with a leading national builder and a substantial pipeline of future work.
  • Competitive Salary: Attractive remuneration reflective of your experience and capability.
  • Additional Earnings: Paid Saturday work available through a rostered arrangement.
  • Strong Project Team: Work alongside experienced construction professionals within a well resourced delivery team.
  • Long Term Location: Ongoing project opportunities in the Osborne precinct, offering consistency for candidates based in Adelaide's northern and western suburbs.
Apply Now If you're an experienced Site Manager looking to take ownership of a significant construction package on one of South Australia's major defence infrastructure projects, we'd welcome a confidential conversation.

Click Apply Now or contact Blair Hickman at Design & Build Recruitment to discuss the opportunity in confidence.

All applications will be treated with strict confidentiality.

job.title: Mental Injury Liability Advisor (MILA).
job.description:
Mental Injury Liability Advisor
  • Multiple permanent opportunities available
  • WorkCover Queensland
  • $96,000 + Superannuation
  • 36.25-hour working week
  • Flexible working arrangements following onboarding
  • Structured training, development and ongoing capability support
ABOUT THE ROLE
Public Sector People are partnering with WorkCover Queensland to recruit multiple Mental Injury Liability Advisors into a newly created specialist function.
These are permanent opportunities offering a salary of $96,000 + superannuation.
  
This is not simply a traditional claims administration role.

We are looking for professionals who can investigate complex matters, review and weigh evidence, apply legislation and policy, make balanced and defensible decisions and confidently communicate those outcomes to workers and employers.

The role will predominantly assess mental injury workers' compensation claims, reviewing medical, factual and workplace information to make timely and evidence-based liability decisions which are clearly documented and capable of withstanding external review, dispute or regulatory scrutiny. 

You will be working with potentially vulnerable customers in sensitive and challenging circumstances, making resilience, empathy, objectivity and strong communication skills particularly important.

You don't necessarily need to come directly from workers' compensation.
We are interested in hearing from candidates across claims, legal, government decision-making, investigations, regulatory, compliance, complaints, dispute resolution and injury-management backgrounds who have strong transferable skills.
  
BENEFITS OF THE ROLE
  • Multiple permanent positions available
  • $96,000 + Superannuation  
  • Newly created specialist mental injury function
  • 36.25-hour working week
  • Flexible working arrangements following initial onboarding
  • Structured training and onboarding
  • Ongoing professional and capability development
  • Supportive leadership structure
  • Genuine long-term career development opportunities
  • Opportunity to undertake meaningful work supporting workers and employers
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
  • Assess and determine liability for workers' compensation claims, predominantly involving mental injuries.
  • Gather, review and analyse detailed medical, factual, workplace and other relevant information.
  • Apply legislation, policy and relevant frameworks to reach balanced and evidence-based decisions.
  • Make timely decisions that are well reasoned, clearly documented and capable of withstanding external review, dispute or regulatory scrutiny.
  • Communicate decisions professionally and empathetically, including sensitive, complex and potentially adverse outcomes.
  • Engage effectively with workers, employers, treating providers and other relevant stakeholders.
  • Influence positive return-to-work and recovery outcomes while liability is being determined.
  • Work professionally with vulnerable customers and sensitive mental injury matters.
  • Review large volumes of information and identify the evidence most relevant to a decision.
  • Prepare clear and accurate written documentation explaining decisions and outcomes.
  • Work collaboratively across the wider claims function to support a smooth customer journey.
  • Contribute to the continued development of this newly created specialist function.
SELECTION CRITERIA
  • Demonstrated experience assessing complex information and reaching evidence-based decisions.
  • Strong analytical, investigative and problem-solving skills.
  • Strong written communication skills with the ability to clearly document reasoning and decisions.
  • Experience applying legislation, regulation, policy or another structured decision-making framework.
  • Ability to interpret and summarise large volumes of complex information.
  • Ability to communicate complex or difficult decisions clearly and professionally.
  • High levels of resilience and professionalism when dealing with sensitive subject matter.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to demonstrate empathy while maintaining objectivity and sound professional judgement.
  • Comfortable working in an environment undergoing continued change, improvement and development.
  • Ability to manage multiple matters and competing priorities effectively.
RELEVANT CANDIDATE BACKGROUNDS
We are particularly interested in hearing from professionals with backgrounds including:
  • Workers' compensation claims
  • CTP, life insurance or income protection
  • Personal injury or insurance law
  • Junior legal professionals with relevant transferable experience
  • Government assessment or statutory decision-making
  • Regulatory and compliance
  • Investigations
  • Complaints and dispute resolution
  • Injury management and occupational rehabilitation
  • Other professional environments involving evidence assessment, legislation, complex decision-making and difficult customer conversations
Direct workers' compensation experience is not essential where you can demonstrate strong transferable experience.

WHY MAKE THE MOVE?
This is an opportunity to secure a permanent career position within a newly established specialist function.

You will be joining an environment where your ability to analyse information and make evidence-based decisions has a genuine impact on workers, employers and recovery outcomes.

For candidates coming from legal, insurance, regulatory, investigations or government environments, this also provides an opportunity to apply your existing skills within a new specialist career pathway.

APPLY NOW
Please apply with a WORD copy of your CV.

If you would like to discuss these multiple permanent Mental Injury Liability Advisor opportunities in more detail, or would like a confidential conversation about whether your experience is transferable to the role, please contact:

Paul Johanson
QLD State Manager | Public Sector People
T: 0401 857 515
E: pjohanson@publicsectorpeople.com.au

job.title: Site Supervisor
job.description:
Contract Site Supervisor - Commercial Construction (Strong Path to Permanent)

Adelaide / Greater Adelaide, South Australia

Our client is a growing, progressive commercial construction and project management company based in South Australia. They specialise in high-quality design & construct, new builds, refurbishments and fit-outs across sectors including commercial, healthcare, education, aged care, hospitality, retail and public works. With a strong pipeline of projects and a reputation for delivering with agility, quality and clear communication, they are seeking an experienced Site Supervisor to join on a contract basis with a genuine likelihood of the role becoming permanent.

The Role
You will be the hands-on site leader responsible for day-to-day delivery. Working closely with the Project Manager and wider team, you will coordinate trades and subcontractors, maintain program, uphold safety and quality standards, and keep projects moving efficiently in live or occupied environments.

Key responsibilities include:
  • Supervising and coordinating daily site activities, trades and subcontractors
  • Leading pre-start / toolbox meetings, site inductions and promoting a strong safety culture
  • Monitoring progress against program, identifying issues early and driving resolution
  • Ensuring works meet drawings, specifications and quality standards
  • Managing site logistics, materials coordination and documentation
  • Maintaining clear communication with the project team, consultants and stakeholders
  • Supporting a professional, collaborative site environment
About You
  • Proven experience as a Site Supervisor (or equivalent) in commercial construction — ideally with a head contractor
  • Strong trade background preferred (carpentry or similar highly regarded)
  • Solid understanding of WHS requirements, safe work methods and site compliance (White Card essential)
  • Ability to read and interpret drawings and specifications
  • Practical, solutions-focused approach with good communication and leadership skills
  • Comfortable working in a fast-paced, collaborative environment and using digital tools
  • Current driver's licence and full working rights in Australia
What's on Offer
  • Initial contract engagement with a clear pathway to permanent employment
  • Competitive contract rates (permanent package to be discussed on conversion)
  • Exposure to a varied and interesting project pipeline
  • Supportive team environment that values quality, initiative and practical problem-solving
  • Opportunity to grow with a company that invests in modern ways of working
This is a strong opportunity for a capable Site Supervisor who wants both immediate site responsibility and a realistic chance of a longer-term role with a forward-thinking builder.
 
To apply:
Please send your CV and a short note outlining your relevant commercial site experience to:

James Jarvis | jjarvis@designandbuild.com.au | 0385353100

job.title: Electrical Estimator
job.description:
Electrical Estimator
Location: Melbourne, Victoria
Company: Tier 1 MEP Contractor
Package: Up to $170k + Super + Car + Benefits
Employment Type: Full-Time, Permanent
 
About the Company
Our client is a leading Tier 1 Mechanical, Electrical and Plumbing (MEP) contractor with an established reputation for delivering complex building services packages across some of Australia's most significant construction projects.
With a strong pipeline of secured and upcoming projects, they are looking to appoint an experienced Electrical Estimator and Senior Estimator to join their Melbourne team.
 
This is an opportunity to work alongside an experienced pre-construction and estimating team, contributing to the delivery of major projects across commercial construction, infrastructure, healthcare, industrial and data centre sectors.
 
The Opportunity
As an Electrical Estimator, you will play a key role in the tendering and pre-construction process, preparing accurate and competitive estimates for large-scale electrical services packages, predominately working on D&C packages.
Working closely with the pre-construction, engineering and project delivery teams, you will be responsible for assessing project requirements, developing cost plans, obtaining subcontractor and supplier pricing, and ensuring tenders are commercially competitive while maintaining project profitability.
You will have exposure to significant projects and the opportunity to contribute to high-value electrical packages from initial tender through to contract award.
 
Key Responsibilities
  • Prepare detailed electrical estimates, cost plans and tender submissions for commercial and major construction projects.
  • Review architectural, electrical and services drawings, specifications and tender documentation.
  • Undertake quantity take-offs and measure electrical materials, labour and equipment requirements.
  • Obtain and evaluate supplier and subcontractor quotations to ensure competitive and accurate pricing.
  • Identify project risks, exclusions, scope gaps and potential value engineering opportunities.
  • Liaise with consultants, suppliers, subcontractors and internal project stakeholders throughout the tender process.
  • Develop and maintain accurate estimating documentation, cost breakdowns and tender comparisons.
  • Work collaboratively with the pre-construction and project delivery teams to ensure a smooth handover following successful tender awards.
  • Assist with tender reviews, commercial negotiations and submission deadlines.
Skills & Experience
  • Previous experience working as an Electrical Estimator within an electrical contractor, MEP contractor or building services environment.
  • Strong understanding of electrical building services, including power distribution, lighting, communications, security, fire and associated infrastructure.
  • Ability to interpret electrical drawings, specifications and technical documentation.
  • Experience undertaking detailed quantity take-offs, cost planning and tender preparation.
  • Strong knowledge of electrical materials, labour costs, subcontractor pricing and procurement processes.
  • Experience pricing commercial, industrial, infrastructure or large-scale construction projects.
  • Strong communication, negotiation and stakeholder management skills.
  • Excellent attention to detail with the ability to manage multiple tenders and competing deadlines.
What's on Offer?
  • Opportunity to join an established Tier 1 MEP contractor, working on Melbourne's best commercial and mission critical construction projects.
  • Exposure to major, technically challenging projects across Melbourne and Victoria.
  • Strong pipeline of secured and upcoming work with long-term stability.
  • A Salary Package of up to $170k + Super + Car + Benefits
  • Long-term career progression to progress into a Pre-Construction Manager or Estimating Manager within a leading building services contractor.
  • Opportunity to develop your experience across major commercial, infrastructure and mission-critical projects within the MEP industry.
Interested?
If you're an experienced Electrical Estimator looking to take the next step in your career and work on some of Melbourne's most significant construction projects, we'd be keen to hear from you.
Apply now or for a confidential discussion please reach out to Connor Gwilliam at cgwilliam@designandbuild.com.au , alternatively call on 0420979409

| Permanent Opportunity | Immediate Start
An established and growing commercial construction business is seeking an experienced Site Manager to take ownership of an industrial new-build project near Geelong.
Operating across Victoria, NSW and Queensland, the business specialises in industrial construction and delivers projects ranging from $3.5M to $25M, with a strong focus on quality, programme and efficient project delivery.
With approximately 160 employees and a growing pipeline of work, this is an opportunity to join a well-established builder that has developed a strong point of difference through its in-house concrete and structural capabilities.
The successful candidate will take full responsibility for managing site operations, coordinating subcontractors and driving the project from commencement through to completion.

The Role
This is a hands-on Site Management position where you will have full ownership of the day-to-day site operations.
Working closely with the Project Manager, engineers and subcontractors, you will be responsible for ensuring the project is delivered safely, efficiently and to a high standard.
Key responsibilities will include:
  • Taking ownership of all site operations from project commencement through to completion and handover.
  • Managing and coordinating subcontractors, trades and site resources to maintain productivity.
  • Developing, managing and driving construction programmes to ensure project milestones are achieved.
  • Planning construction sequencing, site logistics and upcoming activities.
  • Preparing the site and coordinating works around weather conditions and construction requirements.
  • Managing concrete pours and coordinating associated trades and activities.
  • Maintaining high standards of workmanship, quality assurance and construction compliance.
  • Managing site safety, including inductions, SWMS, toolbox talks and regular site inspections.
  • Liaising with engineers, consultants, subcontractors and the wider project team.
  • Identifying potential programme or construction issues and implementing practical solutions.
  • Monitoring subcontractor performance and ensuring works are completed in line with drawings and specifications.
About You
You will be an experienced Site Manager who is confident taking ownership of a project and managing all aspects of site delivery without relying on additional foremen or supervisors.
To be successful, you will ideally have:
  • At least 5 years' experience in a Site Management position.
  • A strong background in new-build construction. Refurbishment-only experience will not be suitable.
  • Previous industrial or commercial construction experience preferred.
  • High-quality residential new-build experience will also be considered.
  • Strong programming, sequencing and construction methodology knowledge.
  • Experience managing subcontractors and coordinating multiple trades on site.
  • A solid understanding of concrete works, site preparation and construction processes.
  • Strong knowledge of OH&S, quality control and site compliance.
  • The ability to work autonomously, make decisions and drive productivity.
  • Excellent communication and leadership skills.
  • A proactive, organised and hands-on approach to site management.
The Working Environment
The business operates with a relatively lean site team, typically coordinating around five subcontractors on site at any one time.
Site Managers are trusted to run their projects and take responsibility for the entire site operation. There are no separate foremen or supervisors, so the successful candidate must be comfortable managing everything from programming and subcontractor coordination through to safety, quality and daily site activities.
The role will suit someone who enjoys being hands-on, takes pride in their work and is comfortable working in a fast-paced construction environment.
Flexibility is important, particularly around concrete pours and critical stages of construction. Candidates should be comfortable working additional hours and Saturdays when required.

What's on Offer?
  • Permanent opportunity with an established commercial and industrial builder.
  • Immediate requirement for an experienced Site Manager.
  • Opportunity to take ownership of an industrial new-build project.
  • Join a business with approximately 160 employees and operations across multiple states.
  • A strong pipeline of industrial construction work.
  • Work within a business with in-house concrete and structural capabilities.
  • Opportunity to build a long-term career with a growing construction business.
Apply Now If you are an experienced Site Manager with a strong new-build background and are looking for a long-term opportunity within an established industrial construction business, we would be interested in speaking with you.
All applications and enquiries will be treated confidentially.

You will be responsible for independently managing the commercial and contractual administration of approximately three projects, working alongside the wider project team to ensure strong commercial outcomes.
The role requires someone who is confident managing the day-to-day CA function, particularly subcontract procurement, head contract administration, cost forecasting and progress claims.

  • Experience administering head contracts.

  • Experience with project cost forecasting and generating commercial reports.

You will be joining an established Australian commercial builder with a long-standing presence in the Victorian construction market and a diverse portfolio of completed and ongoing projects.

job.title: Executive Assistant to the CEO
job.description:
Public Sector People are partnering with a local government organisation to recruit for an Executive Assistant the CEO.
  
Contract: 3 months | Immediate Start
Hourly Pay Rate: $86 p/h + Super
  
Responsibilities: 
  • Provide high-level executive and business support to the Chief Executive Officer (CEO), delivering a professional, responsive and customer-focused service to the Executive and Management Teams and external stakeholders.
  • Liaise closely with the Lord Mayor’s Office to ensure alignment and consistency on key matters, while identifying and managing potential political and reputational risks.
  • Coordinate the flow of communication between the CEO, Executive Directors, Group Managers, Council staff and external stakeholders, ensuring matters are addressed efficiently and resolved in a timely manner.
  • Prepare and coordinate high-quality executive briefs, submissions, reports, correspondence, presentations and other documentation, undertaking research as required.
  • Build and maintain strong relationships with internal and external stakeholders, ensuring the CEO is kept informed of key issues, developments and sensitive matters.
  • Proactively manage and escalate complex or sensitive issues, including those of a political or reputational nature, working collaboratively with relevant teams to achieve appropriate outcomes.
  • Manage the CEO’s calendar, prioritise appointments and coordinate executive meetings to ensure effective time management and scheduling.
  • Oversee CEO correspondence, including receiving, recording, acknowledging and responding to communications within required timeframes.
  • Maintain accurate records, databases and information management systems, ensuring compliance with organisational policies and procedures.
  • Contribute to the development and improvement of administrative systems, processes and business practices, as well as coordinate special projects and initiatives as directed by the CEO.
  • Provide general executive administration support, including minute taking, meeting coordination, travel arrangements, conference bookings, training and stationery management.
  • Coordinate all administrative requirements for CEO meetings, including preparing and distributing agendas, taking minutes, managing follow-up actions and organising hospitality for visitors.
  • Welcome and assist visitors, screen incoming telephone calls and proactively research and resolve enquiries on behalf of the CEO where possible.
  
Essential:
  • Local government experience.
  • Previous experience with TechOne, Content Manager/TRIM, Authority or Pathway highly regarded
  • Proven experience in providing high level executive, secretarial and business support services to
    chief executive officers or senior executives.
  • 5 plus years’ experience in a similar position
  • Demonstrated experience communicating with a range of senior Executives and Councilors or Board members with diverse, competing and complex needs.
  
For a confidential discussion, please contact Chloe Dallimore at cdallimore@publicsectorpeople.com.au
  
Public Sector People is an equal opportunity employer. We embrace diversity and inclusion and are committed to creating a work environment that is supportive and empowering for all. We encourage qualified candidates of all backgrounds to apply.
  
To learn more about Public Sector People and our commitment to driving positive change in the public sector, please visit our website: https://www.publicsectorpeople.com.au

job.title: Senior Project Manager | Commercial Construction
job.description:
Melbourne | Tier 3 Builder | Education, Healthcare & Community Projects
An opportunity is available for an experienced Senior Project Manager to join an established and growing commercial construction business with a strong reputation for delivering quality projects across Victoria.
With a diverse portfolio spanning education, healthcare, aged care, community, recreation and commercial construction, this is an opportunity to join a business with an established pipeline of work and a collaborative, delivery-focused culture.
The business delivers projects predominantly across the $1m–$15m range, with an increasing focus on larger and more complex developments. They offer an environment where experienced construction professionals are trusted to take ownership, make decisions and play an important role in the ongoing success of the business.

The Opportunity
Reporting into senior leadership, you will take responsibility for the successful delivery of multiple commercial construction projects, overseeing all aspects from pre-construction through to completion and handover.
Working closely with Site Managers, Contract Administrators, subcontractors, consultants and clients, you will ensure projects are delivered safely, commercially and in line with agreed programmes and quality expectations.

Key Responsibilities
  • Manage projects from pre-construction and procurement through to practical completion and handover.
  • Oversee project budgets, cost reporting, forecasting and financial performance.
  • Lead procurement activities, subcontractor negotiations and contract administration.
  • Develop and manage construction programmes, ensuring key milestones are achieved.
  • Coordinate Site Managers, Contract Administrators, consultants and subcontractors.
  • Maintain strong relationships with clients, architects, engineers and key stakeholders.
  • Monitor quality assurance, safety and compliance across all project stages.
  • Identify and manage project risks, variations, delays and construction challenges.
  • Provide regular project updates and reporting to senior management.
  • Drive accountability, collaboration and high standards across project teams.
About You
You will be an experienced Project Manager or Senior Project Manager with a background in commercial construction and the ability to independently manage projects from start to finish.
Ideally, you will bring:
  • Proven experience delivering commercial construction projects as a PM or SPM.
  • Exposure to education, healthcare, aged care, community, recreation or institutional projects.
  • Strong commercial acumen, including budgeting, forecasting, procurement and subcontractor management.
  • The ability to lead and coordinate project teams while maintaining strong client relationships.
  • A thorough understanding of construction programmes, contracts, quality and safety requirements.
  • Excellent communication, negotiation and problem-solving skills.
  • A proactive approach, strong work ethic and the ability to take ownership of outcomes.
  • Relevant tertiary qualifications in Construction Management, Building or a related discipline.
The Business & What's on Offer
You will be joining an established Australian commercial builder with decades of industry experience and a diverse portfolio of projects across Victoria.
The business offers:
  • A stable pipeline of varied commercial construction projects.
  • A collaborative and supportive leadership team.
  • A close-knit environment where individuals have genuine responsibility and influence.
  • The opportunity to work across a variety of project sectors rather than being restricted to one market.
  • A business that values integrity, accountability, teamwork and long-term relationships.
  • The opportunity to contribute to the continued growth and success of the business.
Apply Now If you're an experienced Project Manager or Senior Project Manager looking for a new opportunity with an established commercial builder where you can take ownership of projects and make a genuine contribution, we'd be interested in hearing from you.
For a confidential discussion, please get in touch to find out more about the opportunity.
All enquiries and applications will be treated confidentially.

job.title: Procurement Coordinator | Equipment Hire
job.description:
Join an established equipment hire business and take ownership of high-volume purchasing and CAPEX coordination across a national branch network.

The Opportunity
Our client is a well-established Australian equipment hire business with an extensive branch network and a fleet of more than 15,000 assets.
With over 1,000 new and replacement assets purchased annually, they are seeking an organised, commercially minded Procurement / Purchasing Officer to coordinate purchasing activities, manage CAPEX requests and ensure equipment is delivered efficiently across the business.

This is a hands-on, high-volume role suited to someone who thrives in a fast-paced environment, enjoys working with multiple stakeholders and has a strong eye for detail.

Working alongside experienced asset management, operations and finance teams, you'll play a key role in ensuring purchasing processes run smoothly, budgets are controlled and branches have the equipment they need.

Key Responsibilities
  • Manage the end-to-end CAPEX request process, from initial branch requests through to approval, purchasing and delivery.
  • Coordinate high volumes of equipment purchases across a large branch network.
  • Maintain accurate purchasing registers, tracking requests, approvals, orders, deliveries and asset allocations.
  • Raise purchase orders and liaise with suppliers regarding pricing, availability and delivery timeframes.
  • Monitor purchasing expenditure and ensure compliance with CAPEX budgets and internal approval processes.
  • Build and maintain strong supplier relationships, negotiating pricing and identifying cost-saving opportunities.
  • Work closely with Branch Managers, Operations, Asset Management and Finance to coordinate purchasing requirements.
  • Support equipment allocation, asset transfers, warranty matters and disposal processes.
  • Prepare regular purchasing, CAPEX and asset reporting for management.
  • Identify opportunities to improve purchasing processes, reporting and operational efficiencies.
About You

To be successful in this role, you'll bring:
  • Previous experience in a Procurement Officer, Purchasing Officer, Procurement Coordinator or similar position.
  • Experience managing high volumes of purchasing requests, purchase orders and supplier transactions.
  • Exposure to CAPEX processes, budget tracking or asset management would be highly regarded.
  • Strong Excel skills, with the ability to manage large datasets and maintain accurate reporting.
  • Experience using procurement, ERP or asset management systems.
  • Excellent organisational skills, attention to detail and the ability to manage competing priorities.
  • Strong communication skills and confidence working with suppliers and internal stakeholders.
  • A proactive, solutions-focused approach and the ability to work independently.
Experience within equipment hire, construction machinery, fleet management, transport, civil construction or another asset-intensive industry will be highly regarded.

What's on Offer?
  • $85,000–$105,000 + super, depending on experience.
  • Join an established Australian business with a significant equipment fleet and branch network.
  • A hands-on role offering variety, autonomy and exposure across the wider business.
  • ASAP start - this side of Christmas! 
For any questions relating to this role or other opportunities with D&B and our clients please contact Renee Hamilton at rhamilton@designandbuild.com.au or click apply. Your application will be treated as strictly confidential

job.title: Financial Accountant
job.description:
Financial Accountant
Temporary contract | ASAP Start till end March 2027
Local Council Western Suburbs
38 hours p/week | Hybrid WFH arrangement
$55.58 p/hour + super

Our client, a Local Council in the western suburbs of Melbourne are looking for a Financial Accountant to take ownership of its asset accounting and play a hands-on role in statutory reporting, cashflow and investments. Reporting to the Coordinator Accounting Services, you will help keep the integrity of Council’s financial data front and centre.

If you have a strong technical grounding in asset accounting and a taste for the annual audit, this one is worth a look.

Key responsibilities
  • Own asset accounting, including maintaining asset registers for land, furniture, equipment and plant
  • Apply AASB 116, AASB 13, AASB 136, AASB 1051 and other relevant standards to Council’s asset base, including valuations, depreciation and impairment
  • Support the Coordinator Accounting Services with the Annual Financial Statements and audit information requirements
  • Manage cash receipting, investments, banking and bank reconciliations
  • Prepare cashflow forecasts and recommend ways to maximise investment returns within Council’s Investment Policy
  • Assist with tax compliance, including FBT and BAS returns
  • Complete monthly reconciliations of subsidiary ledgers and the general ledger
  • Identify and implement process and internal control improvements across the finance unit
  • Provide specialist financial advice to business unit managers and staff

About you
  • Tertiary qualification in Accounting or Commerce, with progress toward CPA or CA membership
  • Relevant experience in financial or management accounting and/or financial systems
  • Strong knowledge of accounting standards in a local government context, particularly AASB 116, AASB 13, AASB 136 and AASB 1051, among others
  • Hands-on asset accounting experience, such as revaluations, capitalisation, depreciation and impairment
  • Proficiency in Excel, with experience in an integrated corporate finance system (database query language is an advantage)
  • TechnologyOne experience in the Asset module is highly preferred
  • Strong written and verbal communication with staff at all levels, auditors and statutory bodies
  • Current valid Victorian driver’s licence

job.title: Facilities Manager
job.description:
About the Organisation
PSP is supporting a purpose-driven organisation providing housing solutions that support people and communities across Australia. With a focus on delivering quality housing and positive resident outcomes, the organisation manages a diverse portfolio spanning social housing, affordable housing and Specialist Disability Accommodation (SDA).

This is an opportunity to join an organisation where property and facilities management plays an important role in ensuring residents have access to safe, functional and well-maintained homes. Working collaboratively with a broader Property Services team, you will contribute to the ongoing performance of a significant residential asset and help establish strong operational foundations from the outset.

About the Role
The Facilities Manager is responsible for the day-to-day operation, maintenance and presentation of a high-profile, 27-storey mixed-use residential building in Perth CBD, comprising 219 apartments across social housing, affordable housing and SDA.

Reporting to the Manager, Corporate Assets, you will take ownership of onsite facilities operations, working closely with the wider WA Property Services team to coordinate maintenance, manage contractors and ensure building services and infrastructure operate safely, efficiently and in line with relevant compliance requirements.

With the building preparing to open, this is an opportunity to be involved from the early stages, commencing approximately six weeks before opening to help establish maintenance processes, coordinate contractors and ensure the building is operationally ready.

The role offers a broad mix of responsibilities across building infrastructure, preventative and responsive maintenance, defect management, inspections and upgrades. You will oversee contractor performance across essential services, monitor compliance, maintain asset and maintenance records, manage operating expenditure and respond to issues as they arise.

You will also work closely with Housing Officers and the Allocations team to coordinate repairs and maintenance across individual dwellings, including vacate inspections, while helping maintain a positive experience for residents.

This is a hands on, site-based opportunity for someone who enjoys taking ownership, solving practical problems and ensuring a building is maintained to a high standard. You will have the autonomy to manage day-to-day operations while working collaboratively with an established property team.

About You
You are an experienced facilities or property professional with a strong understanding of building infrastructure, maintenance and contractor management. You enjoy being close to the operational side of a building and are confident coordinating competing priorities in a live residential environment.

You bring experience managing preventative and reactive maintenance, overseeing contractors and service providers, identifying defects and ensuring issues are followed through to resolution. You understand the importance of building compliance, workplace health and safety and maintaining accurate asset and maintenance records.

You will be organised, proactive and comfortable working autonomously, with the communication skills to build effective relationships with contractors, internal stakeholders and residents. You can manage day-to-day operational challenges while maintaining a strong focus on safety, service delivery and building presentation.

Residential apartment or mixed use building experience will be highly regarded, as will exposure to social housing, affordable housing, SDA or other residential environments supporting people with diverse needs. 

This role would strongly suit:
  • A Facilities Manager with experience managing high-density residential apartment buildings or mixed-use developments.
  • A residential property or facilities professional experienced in contractor coordination, building maintenance and defect management.
  • A building operations professional with a strong understanding of essential services, compliance and preventative maintenance.
  • A facilities or property professional from a community housing, affordable housing, SDA or other residential environment looking to take ownership of a significant building.
Relevant qualifications in facilities management, building services, property, engineering, a trade or a related discipline are desirable. A current driver's licence is required, along with the ability to complete relevant employment screening checks.

The Opportunity
This is an opportunity to take ownership of facilities operations within a significant residential building, playing a key role in preparing the asset for opening and establishing effective day-to-day maintenance and contractor management processes.

You will join a collaborative property team and contribute to maintaining a safe, functional and welcoming environment for residents across a diverse mixed tenure housing model.

After-hours work is expected to be minimal and will be remunerated in accordance with the applicable arrangements.

Location: Perth CBD.

Application Process
For a confidential discussion or to receive further information about the opportunity, please contact Sarah Kettlewell 03 8535 3111 at Public Sector People.

job.title: Coordinator Open Space and Environment
job.description:
About Bayside City Council

Bayside City Council is one of Melbourne's most attractive coastal municipalities, known for its beautiful beaches, parks, open spaces and vibrant local communities.
  
Council is committed to delivering high-quality services, protecting its unique natural environment and creating welcoming, connected and liveable spaces for residents and visitors.
  
This presents an exciting opportunity for an experienced open space and environmental professional to play a key leadership role in shaping Bayside's future, enhancing its valued public spaces and delivering positive outcomes for the community.
  
About the Role

Reporting to the Manager Open Space and Recreation, you will lead a multidisciplinary team responsible for the strategic planning, development and delivery of open space, environmental and sustainability programs across Bayside.
  
A key focus will be developing and implementing strategies and policies relating to open space planning, biodiversity, coastal management, environmental sustainability and climate resilience, ensuring Council's priorities are translated into practical outcomes for the community.
  
You will oversee a diverse portfolio of strategic initiatives and projects, balancing environmental protection, community expectations and long-term planning priorities. This includes guiding open space development, managing capital projects and ensuring programs are delivered effectively within agreed budgets and timeframes.
  
The role also has significant stakeholder engagement responsibilities, working closely with Councillors, community groups, environmental volunteers, government agencies and internal teams to build strong relationships and support informed decision-making.
  
Importantly, you will provide leadership and direction to a team of technical specialists, building capability, encouraging collaboration and driving continuous improvement across the service.
  
About You

You are an experienced open space or environmental management professional who combines strong strategic and technical expertise with the people leadership skills required to manage a diverse portfolio.
  
You will bring a sound understanding of open space planning, environmental management, biodiversity or climate resilience, ideally gained within local government or a comparable environment.
  
Experience developing strategies, policies and programs that balance environmental priorities with community needs will be highly regarded. A strong background in project delivery, contract management and budgeting will enable you to confidently oversee competing priorities and deliver sustainable, high-quality outcomes.
  
Importantly, you will be a collaborative and approachable leader who enjoys developing people, building team capability and creating a positive, accountable and supportive working environment.
  
Strong communication and stakeholder engagement skills will be essential, along with the ability to navigate complex issues, influence outcomes and build trusted relationships with Councillors, community groups and external agencies.
  
Tertiary qualifications in Environmental Management, Natural Resource Management, Horticultural Science, Parks Management or a related discipline will be required.
  
Application Process

Public Sector People is partnering with Bayside City Council to recruit this opportunity on behalf of the Open Space and Recreation team.
  
For a confidential discussion or to request a copy of the position description, please contact Blanche Grimaux at Public Sector People.
  
To apply, please submit your CV and a brief cover letter via the link.
  
Applications close Monday 1st December 2026.

job.title: Senior Safety & Wellbeing Business Partner
job.description:
Senior Safety & Wellbeing Business Partner
Hervey Bay, QLD | Salary up to $119,126 + 12% superannuation (IFA 6)

Public Sector People are proud to partner with Fraser Coast Regional Council to recruit an experienced Senior Safety & Wellbeing Business Partner.

This is an opportunity to join Council's People, Safety & Wellbeing function at an important time, supporting meaningful improvements to workplace safety across a large and diverse organisation.

With operations spanning water, waste management, construction, regulatory services, community facilities and customer-facing services, Council offers a varied environment where safety professionals can apply their expertise while developing experience across different operational areas.

Working closely with operational leaders and employees, you will provide specialist WHS advice, support the management of workplace risks and help build practical, sustainable safety practices.

Council recognises that no single safety professional can be an expert in every operational environment. This role offers the opportunity to contribute your individual strengths while working collaboratively within a team that brings together complementary experience and expertise.

The Opportunity
As a Senior Safety & Wellbeing Business Partner, you will work directly with operational teams to provide practical, solutions-focused safety advice and support.

You will play an important role in understanding the different risks and challenges across Council's operations, supporting leaders to implement effective safety practices and strengthening organisational safety capability.

The role will involve a combination of hands-on operational engagement, technical advice, risk management and continuous improvement.

You will also contribute to improvements in Council's safety systems, processes and documentation, supporting a longer-term approach to strengthening workplace safety.
  
Key responsibilities will include:
  • Partnering with operational leaders and employees to provide specialist WHS advice, guidance and support
  • Building strong relationships across Council's diverse operational environments
  • Identifying, assessing and managing workplace health and safety risks
  • Conducting workplace inspections, risk assessments and safety reviews
  • Supporting workplace incident investigations, reporting and corrective actions
  • Providing advice on WHS legislation, regulatory requirements and Council policies
  • Supporting the identification and management of psychosocial hazards and workplace wellbeing risks
  • Contributing to improvements in safety management systems, procedures and recordkeeping
  • Developing practical safety solutions suited to different operational environments
  • Supporting the delivery of WHS training, education and awareness initiatives
  • Coaching and educating leaders and employees to strengthen safety capability and accountability
  • Working collaboratively with other safety professionals to share expertise and deliver consistent outcomes
  • Identifying opportunities for continuous improvement across safety practices and processes
  • Promoting a positive, proactive and solutions-focused safety culture
About You
You will be an experienced WHS professional who enjoys working directly with people, understanding operational challenges and finding practical ways to improve workplace safety.

You will bring sound technical knowledge, strong relationship-building skills and the ability to communicate safety requirements clearly and effectively.

Importantly, you don't need to have worked across every industry represented within Council. You may bring particular strengths in areas such as construction, infrastructure, utilities, high-risk operations, customer-facing environments or psychosocial safety.

Council is interested in professionals who can contribute their expertise, collaborate with others and demonstrate a genuine willingness to learn and develop.

You'll bring:
  • Experience in a WHS advisory, business partnering or similar safety-focused position
  • Sound knowledge of WHS legislation, risk management and contemporary safety practices
  • Experience supporting workplace inspections, risk assessments and incident investigations
  • Strong communication, consultation and stakeholder engagement skills
  • The ability to build relationships and influence safety behaviours across operational teams
  • A practical, adaptable and solutions-focused approach to workplace safety
  • Strong analytical, investigative and problem-solving capability
  • An understanding of psychosocial hazards and workplace wellbeing responsibilities
  • Experience contributing to safety management systems, procedures and continuous improvement
  • The ability to manage competing priorities and work collaboratively across different business areas
  • A proactive approach to professional development and knowledge sharing
  • A genuine commitment to improving workplace safety and supporting others
You will also hold:
  • An AQF Level 5 Diploma in Work Health and Safety, supported by significant relevant experience
  • Demonstrated experience in a WHS advisory or comparable safety role
Previous experience within local government or operational environments such as construction, infrastructure, utilities or community services will be highly regarded.

Council also welcomes applications from candidates with transferable safety experience, the right attitude and a willingness to broaden their expertise.

Why Fraser Coast Regional Council?
Fraser Coast Regional Council serves the communities of Hervey Bay, Maryborough and surrounding areas, offering an attractive coastal lifestyle alongside a diverse and rewarding professional environment.

With a broad range of essential services and operational activities, Council provides safety professionals with the opportunity to develop their expertise, work with different business areas and make a genuine contribution to employee wellbeing.

This role offers the opportunity to join a safety function focused on building stronger partnerships, improving systems and developing practical approaches to workplace safety.

The role offers:
  • A rewarding senior safety business partnering opportunity
  • Salary up to $119,126 + 12% superannuation under an Individual Flexibility Agreement (IFA 6)
  • Ten-day fortnight under IFA arrangements
  • Four weeks' annual leave plus five days' additional recreation leave per year under IFA arrangements
  • Council vehicle for business use only 
  • Long service leave accessible on a pro-rata basis after five years, subject to applicable conditions
  • Professional development and leadership development opportunities
  • Generous study assistance scheme
  • Access to Council's Employee Assistance Program
  • Paid parental leave and emergency services leave
  • Uniform subsidy and employee recognition initiatives
  • A values-based organisational culture
  • Modern administration facilities overlooking the beach
  • The opportunity to broaden your safety experience across diverse operational environments
  • An attractive coastal lifestyle in the Fraser Coast region
This is an opportunity for a safety professional who enjoys being involved in the day-to-day operations of a business and wants to contribute to meaningful improvements in workplace safety.

If you are a proactive, engaging WHS professional looking to broaden your experience and make a genuine impact, we would like to hear from you.

job.title: Construction Programmer / Planner
job.description:
This role will provide specialist construction programming advice, independent programme reviews and practical scheduling support across a portfolio of building construction projects.
  
Working closely with project delivery teams and senior stakeholders, you will play a key role in improving programme reliability, identifying potential delivery delays, managing programme risks and strengthening scheduling capability across the organization.
  
Key Responsibilities
  • Develop and implement standard construction programme templates covering planning, design, approvals, procurement, construction and handover.
  • Develop and maintain integrated master schedules across a portfolio of infrastructure projects.
  • Review project programmes prepared by project managers, contractors and external consultants to ensure accuracy, completeness and realistic delivery timeframes.
  • Identify critical path issues, scheduling constraints, emerging delays and opportunities to improve project delivery.
  • Analyze resource demands across internal teams, consultants, contractors and supply chains.
  • Assess alternative construction sequencing, recovery strategies and acceleration measures.
  • Conduct independent reviews of Extension of Time (EOT) assessments, including critical path impacts, overlapping delays and mitigation measures.
  • Provide practical recommendations to improve programme performance and reduce delivery risks.
  • Deliver training, coaching and guidance to project teams on construction programming and the effective use of Microsoft Project.
  • Identify recurring programme issues and recommend improvements to scheduling processes, documentation and reporting.
  
Successful Candidate
The successful candidate will have demonstrated experience in construction planning and scheduling, particularly across building construction and infrastructure projects.
  
You will have strong technical expertise in developing integrated master schedules, reviewing contractor programmes, analyzing construction delays and assessing critical path impacts. Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Project, combined with a sound understanding of construction methodologies, sequencing and project delivery requirements, is essential.
  
You will also possess strong communication and stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to translate complex programme analysis into clear, practical recommendations. Experience providing guidance, coaching or training to project delivery teams will be highly regarded.
  
This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced construction programmer or planner to provide specialist expertise across a significant government infrastructure portfolio. If interested, send your application through to: daniel@publicsectorpeople.com.au & give me a call on 0466265446 today to discuss this opportunity in further detail!

  • Experience supporting cyber security incident investigation, response, and remediation.

job.title: Senior Integration and Automation Specialist
job.description:
Senior Integration & Automation Specialist
Location: Inner West, Sydney NSW
Work Type: Full Time
Hours: 35-hour week
Salary: $122,063 – $137,421 per annum + 12% superannuation. An additional market allowance may be negotiated, depending on skills, qualifications and experience.

Public Sector People is proud to be partnering with Inner West Council to appoint a Senior Integration & Automation Specialist.

This is an exciting opportunity to establish and shape a new Integration & Automation capability within Council's Digital Services team, with genuine scope to influence the technology, standards and ways of working from the ground up.

Council is looking for someone who enjoys both the technical and people side of integration and automation. Someone who can engage with stakeholders, understand business challenges, design practical solutions and remain hands-on in bringing them to life.

Working within a supportive and forward-thinking team, you'll have the opportunity to contribute to modern integration architecture, explore emerging technologies and deliver innovative solutions that improve how Council operates and provides services to its community.

The Opportunity

You'll play a key role in developing Council's Integration & Automation capability, combining hands-on technical delivery with solution design, stakeholder engagement and technical leadership.

Working closely with business areas, Digital Services teams and external partners, you'll lead conversations to understand business needs, challenge existing approaches and identify opportunities for integration, automation and improvement.

You'll take ownership of solutions from initial discovery and design through to development, implementation and ongoing support, ensuring they are secure, scalable and fit for purpose.


Key responsibilities will include:
  • Designing, developing and implementing enterprise integrations, APIs and automation solutions across Council's systems and platforms.
  • Engaging with stakeholders to understand business challenges, explore options and translate requirements into practical technical solutions.
  • Applying modern integration architecture principles, including API-led, event-driven, message-based and workflow integration patterns.
  • Establishing reusable integration standards, frameworks and practices to support a growing capability.
  • Working collaboratively with vendors, implementation partners and internal teams to deliver effective outcomes.
  • Providing technical leadership, mentoring and guidance while remaining actively involved in hands-on delivery.
  • Exploring opportunities to apply AI, intelligent automation and emerging technologies to improve processes and service delivery.
About You

We're looking for an experienced integration and automation professional who combines strong hands-on technical capability with a consultative approach, sound solution design skills and the confidence to take ownership.

You'll enjoy working directly with stakeholders to understand their challenges, asking the right questions and exploring solutions rather than simply working from a technical specification.

Equally, you'll be someone who still enjoys building, troubleshooting and delivering solutions, with the ability to balance technical considerations with broader business needs.

You'll bring:

  • Strong hands-on experience designing, developing and supporting enterprise integrations, APIs and automation solutions.
  • Experience with Azure Integration Services, Microsoft Power Platform or comparable integration and automation technologies.
  • Sound understanding of modern integration architecture, API management, integration patterns, security and governance.
  • Hands-on development experience across scripting, coding, workflow automation and integration technologies.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement and consulting skills, with experience leading discovery discussions, gathering requirements and translating business challenges into technical solutions.
  • The ability to assess technical options, explain risks and trade-offs, and communicate effectively with technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Experience working with vendors, delivery partners and multidisciplinary teams.
  • Demonstrated initiative, accountability and technical leadership, with the ability to mentor others and influence technical decisions.
  
You'll also be curious about how AI is changing integration, automation and software delivery, including how AI-assisted development, intelligent automation and agents can complement traditional integration and workflow technologies. Practical experience is highly regarded, but not essential.

Experience integrating enterprise platforms such as TechnologyOne, Dynamics 365, ESRI or other SaaS applications would also be valuable.

You don't need to have held a formal Integration Architect or people management position. This opportunity could suit a Senior Integration Engineer, Integration Consultant, Technical Lead or emerging Solution Architect who remains hands-on and is looking to take the next step in their career.

Above all, Council is looking for someone who is curious, collaborative and willing to challenge existing approaches, explore new ideas and take considered risks to deliver better outcomes.

Why Inner West Council?
  • Greenfield opportunity: Help establish Councils Integration & Automation capability, with genuine input into its direction, architecture and ways of working.
  • Innovation and emerging technology: Contribute to AI-enabled initiatives, intelligent automation and modern digital solutions.
  • Career development: Build on your technical expertise while growing your architecture, stakeholder engagement and leadership capabilities.
  • Meaningful projects: Work on initiatives connecting enterprise systems, data platforms, customer experiences and frontline services.
  • Supportive culture: Join a collaborative Digital Services team with progressive leadership that encourages creativity, new ideas and continuous improvement.
  • Work-life balance: Enjoy a 35-hour working week, flexible working arrangements, access to Fitness Passport and additional leave benefits, including MyLeave and Christmas/New Year grant days.

This is an opportunity for someone who wants to do more than deliver individual integrations. You'll have the chance to help shape how Council approaches integration and automation, influence technical decisions and build solutions that make a genuine difference.

Apply Now
  
For a confidential discussion, please contact:
Esme Lynch – Principal Consultant, Public Sector People
M: 0413 282 765
E: esme@publicsectorpeople.com.au
  
Applications close: 11:59pm, Sunday 22nd November 2026
Please note recruitment activity may commence prior to the closing date.

Senior Project Engineer – High Rise Residential

I am working with a highly regarded property development and construction business who are looking to bring an experienced Senior Project Engineer into their Brisbane team.

With a strong presence across the Queensland property market, this business specialises in the development and delivery of high-quality residential projects. Taking a hands-on approach to both development and construction, they are involved throughout the entire project lifecycle, from land acquisition and feasibility through to design, pre-construction and project delivery.

With a strong pipeline of exciting multi-storey residential developments, they are looking to bring someone on board who can play an important role in the successful delivery of their upcoming projects.

You will be working closely with the wider project team, taking ownership of key engineering and coordination responsibilities across high-rise residential developments, with involvement extending into the pre-construction phase.

The Role:
  • Managing technical aspects of multi-storey residential construction projects.
  • Coordinating consultants, subcontractors, suppliers and design documentation.
  • Reviewing drawings, specifications and resolving design discrepancies.
  • Assisting with construction planning, programming and procurement.
  • Working closely with the project team throughout pre-construction and delivery.
  • Managing QA, ITPs, technical submissions and ensuring compliance with project requirements.
About You:
  • Previous experience as a Project Engineer or Senior Project Engineer within commercial construction.
  • A strong background delivering multi-storey residential projects.
  • Previous pre-construction experience, including design coordination, buildability reviews and procurement.
  • Strong technical knowledge and an understanding of construction methodologies.
  • The ability to coordinate multiple stakeholders and drive project outcomes.
  • Excellent communication, organisation and problem-solving skills.
If you're a Senior Project Engineer with a strong multi-storey residential background and pre-construction experience, I'd be keen to have a confidential conversation.

For any questions relating to this role or other opportunities with D&B and our clients please contact Emily Godward on 0423 923 628 or click apply. Your application will be treated as strictly confidential.

job.title: Site Manager
job.description:
The Company

An established Sydney construction business delivering high-quality residential, commercial and mixed-use projects, including complex refurbishments and adaptive re-use developments.

With a hands-on leadership team and a diverse pipeline of work, the business offers experienced construction professionals genuine ownership of their projects and direct access to senior management.

The Opportunity

An excellent opportunity exists for an experienced Site Manager to join the delivery team on one of two significant construction projects located in Sydney's inner-city suburbs, valued at up to approximately $45M.

You'll take responsibility for day-to-day site operations, leading subcontractors, managing construction programs and ensuring the project is delivered safely, on time and to the required quality standards.

The Role

Your responsibilities will include:
  • Taking overall responsibility for day-to-day site operations
  • Managing subcontractors, trades and site personnel
  • Driving construction programs, sequencing and key milestones
  • Coordinating structure, façade, services and finishes packages
  • Managing site logistics and deliveries within constrained inner-city environments
  • Maintaining high standards of WHS, quality assurance and compliance
  • Reviewing drawings and resolving construction and buildability challenges
  • Coordinating consultants, suppliers and project stakeholders
  • Managing inspections, quality documentation and defect rectification
  • Working closely with the Project Manager to maintain program and project performance
  • Overseeing practical completion, commissioning and handover
About You
  • Proven experience as a Site Manager with an Australian construction company
  • Strong background delivering class 2 projects valued at $20M+ highly regarded
  • Strong understanding of construction methodology, programming and subcontractor coordination
  • Proven ability to lead site teams and manage multiple work fronts
  • Excellent knowledge of WHS, quality assurance and compliance requirements
  • Strong communication, leadership and problem-solving skills
  • Trade background, ideally carpentry, highly regarded
  • A proactive, hands-on approach with a strong focus on quality and delivery
In Return
  • Up to $250,000 + Super, depending on experience
  • Lead one of two construction projects valued at up to approximately $45M
  • Convenient inner-city Sydney project locations
  • Genuine autonomy and ownership of site delivery
  • Work closely with experienced Project Managers and senior leadership
  • Exposure to technically interesting residential and commercial projects
  • Established project teams and construction systems
  • Long-term opportunities across a diverse pipeline of Sydney projects
How to Apply Click Apply and include your CV/resume and project list (Word format preferred).

For a confidential discussion about this opportunity, contact Mitchell Barker on 0423 927 536.

All applications will be treated with strict confidentiality.

job.title: Senior Contract Administrator
job.description:
Senior Contract Administrator 

I am working with a very well-established QLD construction business who are looking to bring an experienced Senior Contracts Administrator into their Brisbane team.

With a strong reputation across the commercial construction industry, this privately owned builder specialises in delivering quality projects across commercial construction, education, healthcare, industrial and hospitality sectors.

They have built their business around strong client relationships, quality workmanship and a hands-on approach to project delivery, with a consistent pipeline of work across South East Queensland.

This is an opportunity for an experienced Senior CA to join a growing team and take ownership of the commercial and contractual aspects of projects from procurement through to final accounts.

Working closely with the Senior Leadership and site teams, you will play a key role in ensuring projects are delivered commercially, efficiently and in line with contractual requirements.

The Role:
  • Manage the full commercial and contractual administration of construction projects from procurement through to completion.
  • Prepare, review and negotiate head contracts, subcontract agreements and scopes of work.
  • Manage variations, progress claims, extensions of time and subcontractor payments.
  • Monitor project costs, budgets, cash flow and overall commercial performance.
  • Build and maintain strong relationships with clients, subcontractors and consultants.
  • Work closely with Project Managers and site teams to identify and manage commercial risks.
  • Oversee procurement processes and ensure contractual obligations are being met.
  • Manage final accounts and project close-out documentation.
About You:
  • Proven experience as a Contracts Administrator or Senior Contracts Administrator within a commercial construction environment.
  • A strong understanding of construction contracts, procurement and subcontractor management.
  • Experience managing projects across commercial, industrial, education, healthcare or high-rise residential sectors.
  • Confident managing variations, claims, cost reporting and contractual negotiations.
  • Strong communication and relationship-building skills, with the ability to work closely with site and project teams.
  • A proactive, commercially minded individual who can take ownership and work autonomously.
  • Relevant tertiary qualifications in Construction Management, Quantity Surveying or a similar discipline will be highly regarded.
For any questions relating to this role or other opportunities with D&B and our clients please contact Emily Godward on 0423 923 628 or click apply. Your application will be treated as strictly confidential.

job.title: Contract Administrator
job.description:

An opportunity is available for an experienced Contract Administrator to join a major infrastructure project in Regional NSW. We are seeking a commercially astute professional with a minimum of 5 years' experience working for a civil construction contractor, ideally within a self-performing business.

You will play a key role in managing the project's commercial and contractual obligations, with responsibility across both downstream subcontract procurement and administration, as well as upstream head contract management.

Key Responsibilities
  • Manage upstream head contract administration, including contractual notices, claims, variations, extensions of time (EOTs) and contractual entitlements.
  • Manage downstream procurement of subcontract packages, including scope development, tendering, evaluation, negotiation and subcontract award.
  • Prepare, negotiate and administer subcontract agreements, ensuring commercial terms and project requirements are clearly defined.
  • Assess and manage subcontractor progress claims, variations and payment schedules.
  • Prepare and manage upstream progress claims, variations and commercial submissions to the client.
  • Monitor project costs, commitments, cash flow, variations and financial forecasts.
  • Identify and manage commercial risks, contractual obligations and opportunities to maximise project outcomes.
  • Work closely with Project Managers, Engineers and site teams to support construction delivery.
  • Maintain accurate commercial reporting, contractual correspondence and project documentation.
Skills & Experience
  • Minimum 5 years' experience in a Contract Administrator role within the civil construction or infrastructure sector.
  • Tertiary qualification in Quantity Surveying, Construction Management and Civil Engineering (or similar) 
  • Strong contractor-side experience, ideally with a self-performing civil contractor.
  • Demonstrated experience managing both downstream subcontract procurement and upstream head contract administration.
  • Strong understanding of head contracts, subcontract agreements, claims, variations, EOTs and commercial risk.
  • Experience managing procurement, tender evaluations, negotiations and subcontractor relationships.
  • Strong commercial acumen and the ability to identify and manage contractual entitlements.
  • Excellent communication, negotiation and stakeholder management skills.
  • Ability to work autonomously while contributing to a broader project delivery team.
 
 For any questions relating to this role or any other opportunities with D&B and our clients, please contact Nathan Halligan on 02 9376 8200 OR nhalligan@designandbuild.com.au or click apply. Your application will be treated as strictly confidential

job.title: Manager Communications & Engagement

Public Sector People are proud to partner with Central Highlands Regional Council to appoint an experienced and forward-thinking Manager Communications & Engagement to a newly created senior leadership position.

This is an opportunity to make a genuine impact, leading how Council communicates its vision, engages with its communities and builds meaningful relationships with stakeholders across the Central Highlands region.

Reporting directly to the Chief Executive Officer, you will have the opportunity to bring together Council's Communications and Community Engagement functions, establishing a unified approach that strengthens trust, improves collaboration and ensures the community's voice is reflected in Council's decisions.

For an experienced communications and engagement leader looking for greater influence, autonomy and the opportunity to shape a function, this position offers the platform to make a lasting difference.

The Role Leading an established team of approximately eight professionals, you will provide the strategic direction, leadership and structure required to successfully integrate Council's Communications and Community Engagement functions.

A key priority will be shaping and delivering Council's new Communications Strategy, while establishing more effective approaches to community consultation, stakeholder engagement and the way feedback is captured, communicated and acted upon.

You will work closely with the CEO, Mayor, elected members and senior leadership team, providing trusted advice on communications, engagement, reputation and emerging issues.

Above all, we are looking for someone who can bring people together, establish a clear strategic direction and translate ideas into meaningful outcomes.

Why Join Central Highlands Regional Council? This is more than an opportunity to lead an established function. It is a chance to influence how a regional council connects with its people and communicates its future.
