This is an excellent opportunity for someone with an architectural background who has developed strong construction knowledge and enjoys being involved in the practical delivery of projects.

The Role
Working closely with Project Managers, Site Managers, architects, consultants and subcontractors, your responsibilities will include:
  • Coordinating architectural and consultant documentation across multiple live construction projects.
  • Acting as the link between the design team and site-based construction teams.
  • Reviewing architectural drawings, specifications and shop drawings to identify discrepancies, clashes and potential buildability issues.
  • Managing RFIs, design queries and technical issues raised by the construction team and subcontractors.
  • Coordinating design amendments and ensuring updated documentation is communicated to relevant stakeholders.
  • Reviewing subcontractor shop drawings and ensuring they align with architectural intent and project requirements.
  • Working closely with subcontractors to resolve technical and design-related queries on site.
  • Identifying design inconsistencies, omissions and potential construction issues before they impact programme or delivery.
  • Attending site meetings and coordinating with the wider project team to ensure design matters are progressing.
  • Monitoring design deliverables and ensuring information is issued in line with construction programmes.
  • Supporting the Construction team with technical advice and practical design solutions throughout the build.
About You
We are looking for someone who understands both the design process and what it takes to deliver a project on site.
To be considered, you will ideally have:
  • A degree or qualification in Architecture, Architectural Technology or a related discipline.
  • Previous experience working as a Design Coordinator, Design Manager, Project Architect or similar within the construction industry.
  • Experience working on multi-residential, apartment, social housing or commercial construction projects.
  • Strong ability to interpret and interrogate architectural drawings, specifications and construction documentation.
  • Experience reviewing and coordinating subcontractor shop drawings.
  • Previous exposure to construction sites and an understanding of construction sequencing and buildability.
  • Confidence communicating with subcontractors, Site Managers, Project Managers, architects and consultants.
  • The ability to identify design issues, find practical solutions and follow them through to resolution.
  • Strong organisational skills and the ability to coordinate multiple projects and competing priorities.
Importantly, this role requires someone who is comfortable being site-based, communicating directly with subcontractors and working alongside the construction team to resolve issues as they arise.

The Business & What’s on Offer
You'll be joining an established Melbourne builder and developer with a strong presence across the residential construction market.
The business has a growing pipeline of projects, with a particular focus on social and affordable housing, build-to-rent and multi-residential developments.
You'll have the opportunity to:
  • Work across multiple projects valued between $30M and $60M.

  • Work closely with experienced Construction Managers and Project Managers.
  • Take ownership of design coordination from early construction through to completion.
  • Have genuine involvement in the practical delivery of projects rather than being confined to an office-based design role.
  • Join a collaborative construction team where design coordination plays an important part in successful project delivery.
Interested?
If you have an architectural background, understand construction documentation and enjoy working closely with site teams to deliver quality projects, we'd love to hear from you.
For a confidential discussion, please get in touch to find out more.

job.title: Manager, Property and Housing
job.description:
Public Sector People are partnering with a large, values-led organisation to appoint a Manager, Property and Housing within its property and assets function.

Reporting to a senior property leader, this position will oversee housing and real estate operations across a diverse portfolio encompassing community housing, residential property and retirement living.

The organisation is reviewing how its wider property function operates, with work underway to strengthen its strategy and create clearer responsibilities across property operations, facilities and asset management. This creates a genuine opportunity for the incoming Manager to help shape the future direction of the function.

The opportunity

You will lead a multidisciplinary team responsible for property and tenancy management, retirement living coordination and independent living unit sales.

The role combines people leadership with hands-on operational oversight. You will bring greater consistency to the function, strengthen processes and reporting, and ensure the team delivers a reliable and responsive service.

Key responsibilities will include:
  • Leading, coaching and supporting a multidisciplinary property team
  • Overseeing community housing, residential tenancy, leasing and retirement living activities
  • Establishing clear priorities, workflows and performance expectations
  • Improving operational systems, procedures, templates and reporting
  • Ensuring compliance with relevant housing, tenancy and retirement living requirements
  • Monitoring operational risks, audits, registers and reporting obligations
  • Working closely with asset management, projects, development, finance and legal teams
  • Supporting internal stakeholders with leasing, occupancy, sales and property matters
  • Providing timely advice and recommendations to senior leaders
  • Contributing to the organisation’s wider property strategy
This is an operational leadership position rather than a capital works role. It will suit someone who enjoys leading people, creating structure and working across several connected areas of housing and property.

About you

You will bring strong experience from property management, community housing, retirement living or another relevant operational property environment.

You do not need to have worked across every part of the portfolio. However, you will need the leadership capability, judgement and adaptability to manage a broad remit within a regulated and service-focused organisation.

You will ideally offer:
  • Experience leading and developing a property or housing team
  • Strong knowledge of residential property or tenancy management
  • Exposure to community housing, social housing or retirement living
  • An understanding of property maintenance and contractor management
  • Experience improving operational systems, processes and reporting
  • Sound knowledge of compliance within a regulated environment
  • Confidence managing complex stakeholders and competing priorities
  • A calm, practical and accountable leadership style
  • Relevant tertiary qualifications in property, real estate or a related discipline
Experience with NCAT, housing management systems and retirement living legislation would be advantageous.

For a confidential discussion, please contact Ebonnie Goss at Public Sector People or apply with an up-to-date resume.

Working closely with builders, designers, engineers, factory personnel and installation teams, you'll play a central role in ensuring projects run smoothly, deadlines are met and clients receive a high level of service.

  • Design & Engineering: Coordinate design and detailing workflows, manage drawing revisions, follow up RFIs and ensure the latest approved documentation is available.
  • Manufacturing: Work alongside the factory team to coordinate production schedules, priorities and manufacturing requirements.
  • Delivery & Logistics: Organise transport, delivery schedules, site access, unloading arrangements and crane requirements.
  • Installation: Coordinate installation crews, mobilisation dates, site readiness and onsite progress.
  • Client Management: Maintain regular communication with builders, clients and internal stakeholders, providing project updates and following up outstanding information.
  • Cost & Variations: Identify scope changes, coordinate variation requests and assist with monitoring project costs.
  • Reporting & Documentation: Maintain project trackers, schedules, drawing registers, approval logs and progress reports.
About You
We're looking for someone who is proactive, exceptionally organised and enjoys working in a fast-paced environment where no two days are the same.
You'll ideally have:
  • Previous experience in project coordination, project administration or a similar role.
  • Exposure to the construction, manufacturing or building products industry.
  • The ability to read and interpret architectural and construction drawings.
  • Strong communication and stakeholder management skills.
  • Excellent organisational skills and the ability to manage competing priorities.
  • Strong attention to detail and confidence using Microsoft Excel, Outlook and project tracking systems.
  • A proactive approach to problem-solving and following up outstanding actions.
Experience with light gauge steel, timber frame and truss manufacturing, structural drawings, BIM models or prefabricated construction would be highly regarded.

A qualification in civil or structural engineering, architecture or construction would also be advantageous.

What's on Offer?
  • Salary package of $85,000 = $100k + Super, depending on experience.
  • Full training provided, including training on the company's software and systems.
  • A progressive career path with opportunities to explore different areas of the wider group business.
  • Exposure to the full project lifecycle, developing both technical and commercial construction knowledge.
  • The opportunity to join an established specialist business and make a genuine contribution to its project delivery operations.

job.title: Manager Roads
job.description:
Manager Roads | Warrumbungle Shire Council | Coonabarabran, NSW

$180,000–$209,000 Total Remuneration Package + Relocation Assistance
  • Lead the operational delivery of a 2,518km road network across regional NSW
  • Attractive remuneration, leaseback vehicle and housing options
  • Relocation assistance up to $7,500 | Exceptional regional lifestyle
The Opportunity
Public Sector People is partnering with Warrumbungle Shire Council to recruit an experienced Manager Roads, offering an opportunity to lead one of Council's most significant operational functions and make a lasting contribution to the region's infrastructure and communities.

Spanning more than 12,000 square kilometres, Warrumbungle Shire is home to welcoming rural communities, spectacular national parks and Australia's first Dark Sky Park.

Reporting to the Director Infrastructure Services, you will oversee the maintenance and operational delivery of Council's 2,518km road network, comprising 975km of sealed and 1,543km of unsealed roads.

This is a hands-on leadership position, combining operational management, financial oversight and contract delivery with the opportunity to build on recent improvements to team culture, maintenance practices and service delivery.

The Role
Leading a team of engineers, supervisors and operational staff, you will be responsible for coordinating Council's extensive roads maintenance programs across a geographically diverse network.

Key responsibilities include:
  • Lead and develop the Roads team, fostering a positive, accountable and safety-focused workplace culture.
  • Oversee sealed and unsealed road maintenance programs, ensuring safe, efficient and consistent service delivery.
  • Manage operational budgets, resources and forward works programs, balancing internal delivery capabilities with external contractors.
  • Oversee Council's Roads Maintenance Council Contract (RMCC) with Transport for NSW, ensuring contractual compliance and effective stakeholder relationships.
  • Manage procurement, tendering, contractor performance and operational reporting.
  • Support the completion of natural disaster recovery projects and emerging infrastructure demands associated with the Central-West Orana Renewable Energy Zone.
  • Build effective relationships across Council, government agencies and the community.
Importantly, this is a working management role. You'll remain closely involved in operational decision-making, financial management and problem-solving, providing practical leadership rather than operating solely at a strategic level.

About You
We're seeking an experienced roads or infrastructure professional who combines strong operational knowledge with the leadership capability to manage a substantial workforce.

Ideally, you will demonstrate:
  • Tertiary qualifications in Civil Engineering, Construction Management or a related discipline, or extensive relevant experience.
  • Demonstrated experience managing roads maintenance programs, ideally within local government or a comparable infrastructure environment.
  • Strong understanding of rural road maintenance practices, particularly unsealed networks.
  • Proven people leadership experience, including developing teams, managing performance and driving continuous improvement.
  • Strong financial acumen and experience managing budgets, contractors, procurement and infrastructure contracts.
  • Excellent communication, stakeholder engagement and problem-solving skills.
  • A proactive approach to WHS, risk management and operational compliance.
Previous NSW local government and RMCC experience will be highly regarded, although candidates from other relevant infrastructure environments are encouraged to apply.

Above all, Council is seeking a visible, collaborative and technically credible leader who can build trust, take ownership and deliver results.

What's on Offer?
  • $180,000–$209,000 total remuneration package ($143,000–$166,000 salary + 3.5% Civil Liability Allowance + 10% Overtime Allowance + Superannuation)
  • Leaseback vehicle option, including private use under Council's arrangements.
  • Relocation assistance up to $7,500 to support your move.
  • Housing option – opportunity to rent a four-bedroom Council property in Coolah.
  • Salary packaging benefits, including eligible rental and household fuel expenses.
  • Flexible and hybrid working arrangements by agreement.
  • Rostered days off, generous leave entitlements and health and wellbeing initiatives.
  • Professional development opportunities and a supportive management environment.
Discover Warrumbungle Shire
Located in the heart of regional NSW, Warrumbungle Shire offers a unique lifestyle surrounded by spectacular natural landscapes, welcoming communities and wide-open spaces.

From the Warrumbungle National Park to internationally recognised dark skies, the region offers an opportunity to escape the pace of metropolitan living while taking on a meaningful leadership position.

With flexibility to work from Coonabarabran or Coolah, this is an opportunity to make a genuine difference while enjoying the benefits of regional life.

How to Apply
Public Sector People is managing this recruitment process on behalf of Warrumbungle Shire Council.
For a confidential discussion, please contact Will Cooke at Public Sector People.

Will Cooke – Senior Consultant
Public Sector People
M: 0412 950 548

Design & Build are partnered with a national contractor that works with Tier 1 Contractors and Builders all over Australia. 

You will be working across a diverse portfolio of technically challenging projects, you will be responsible for developing robust cost estimates, coordinating tender submissions and involved in strategic bidding decisions. 

Key Responsibilities:
  • Lead the preparation of cost plans, estimates and tender submissions from initial review through to final submission.
  • Analyse project requirements, technical documentation and commercial conditions to establish accurate pricing.
  • Develop cost-effective delivery approaches, resource assumptions and project sequencing strategies.
  • Obtain and assess supplier and subcontractor pricing to support competitive bids.
  • Identify commercial risks, pricing gaps and opportunities to improve tender outcomes.
  • Work closely with operational and commercial teams to validate assumptions and develop bid strategies.
  • Maintain accurate estimating records, cost databases and tender documentation.
  • Participate in tender interviews, client discussions and project clarification processes.
Profile:
  • At least five years' experience in estimating within construction, civil works, infrastructure or a related contracting environment.
  • Proven ability to prepare detailed estimates and manage multiple bids concurrently.
  • Strong understanding of construction techniques, resource requirements and project costs.
  • Confident interpreting technical documentation, scopes of work and contractual requirements.
  • Experience working with estimating, cost planning or project scheduling software.
  • Strong commercial judgement, analytical skills and attention to detail.
  • Effective communicator with the ability to build relationships across project teams, clients and subcontractors.
Key Details:
  • This role is full-time in the office, so it would suit people willing to travel near the airport. 

If you are looking for a role where you can take ownership of tenders, please apply.

For any questions relating to this role or any other opportunities with D&B and our clients, please contact Nathan Halligan on 02 9376 8200 OR nhalligan@designandbuild.com.au or click apply. Your application will be treated as strictly confidential

job.title: Manager Planning & Land Management
job.description:
The Manager Planning and Land Management is integral to the ongoing delivery statutory functions of council, ensuring compliance with the relevant legislation and local laws through education then enforcement and the strategic planning for the region. These functions include development assessment, building certification, plumbing, compliance, ranger services, rural land management, and strategic land use.
  
A secondary role of the Manager Planning and Land Management is the Mining liaison officer for council to facilitate discussions regarding new mining operations, extensions to existing operations or plans to cease operations and the post closure aspects.
  
Key Responsibilities
  • Lead and manage the Planning & Land Management team, providing strategic direction and supporting multidisciplinary staff.
  • Oversee development assessment, strategic land use planning and planning scheme amendments.
  • Manage building and plumbing regulation, compliance activities and associated statutory functions.
  • Provide expert advice on Queensland planning legislation, regulations, local laws and relevant codes of practice.
  • Oversee ranger services, animal management, stock routes, rural land practices and environmental health functions.
  • Develop and implement policies, procedures and systems to improve operational efficiency and compliance.
  • Prepare complex reports, provide advice to senior management and elected representatives, and engage with the community and key stakeholders.
  • Manage projects, budgets, resources and service delivery outcomes.
  • Act as the Council's mining liaison officer, facilitating discussions regarding new mining operations, existing operations and mine closure matters.
  • Drive continuous improvement, risk management and a customer-focused approach across the section.
  
Successful Candidate
The successful candidate will be an experienced planning and land management professional with a strong background in local government, proven leadership capabilities and a sound understanding of Queensland's legislative and regulatory environment.
  
You will demonstrate the ability to manage competing priorities, lead multidisciplinary teams and provide practical, professional advice on complex planning and compliance matters.
  
Mandatory requirements
  • Bachelor of Urban and Regional Town Planning or a similar relevant degree.
  • Previous local government experience.
  • Strong knowledge and practical experience applying Queensland planning legislation.
  • Excellent knowledge of legislation, regulations, design standards and codes of practice relating to building, plumbing, planning, animal management and stock routes.
  • Experience across ranger services and rural land management practices.
  • Experience in environmental health practices.
  • Demonstrated leadership, business management and project management capabilities.
  • Experience developing and implementing policies, procedures, planning schemes and compliance processes.
  • Excellent communication, negotiation and stakeholder engagement skills.
  • A minimum of a Queensland C-class provisional driver's license.
  
Desirable
  • Experience using TechOne.
  • Postgraduate qualifications in a relevant discipline.
  • Experience in change management and continuous improvement initiatives.

If you are someone that comes a from strong planning, land use & management background, this is the role for you. Please note this position will be based out of the councils Emerald office location! 

Send your application through to: daniel@publicsectorpeople.com.au & give me a call today to discuss this contract opportunity in further detail!

job.title: Aftercare Maintenance coordinator
job.description:
Commercial Construction | South Melbourne |
Are you a construction professional who enjoys problem-solving, coordinating trades and working with people? This is an opportunity to take your construction knowledge into an Aftercare Maintenance Manager role with an established commercial builder in Melbourne.
With a strong pipeline of projects expected to come through in the new year, the business is looking to strengthen its aftercare team with a practical, organised and people-focused individual who takes pride in getting issues resolved and delivering a positive client experience.

The Opportunity
Working alongside an established aftercare team, you will oversee building defects and maintenance issues across a range of projects, coordinating rectification works and ensuring clients are kept informed throughout the process.
This is a varied role combining administration, client communication, trade coordination and site visits. The position can be tailored towards a more office-based or site-focused approach, depending on your strengths and experience.
Key Responsibilities
  • Manage building defects, maintenance requests and aftercare issues across completed projects.
  • Assess defects and coordinate the appropriate trades to carry out rectification works.
  • Schedule and coordinate trades, monitor progress and follow up on outstanding items.
  • Communicate directly with clients, including private apartment owners, providing regular updates and managing expectations.
  • Arrange site visits, inspect issues and help determine practical solutions.
  • Maintain clear records and ensure aftercare matters are followed through to completion.
  • Work collaboratively with project teams, subcontractors and internal stakeholders to deliver a high standard of service.
About You
You may currently be working in site management, construction supervision, maintenance, defects or aftercare, or have a broader construction background that would translate well into this type of position.
We are interested in people who have:
  • Previous experience in the construction industry and a sound understanding of building defects and rectification works.
  • The ability to identify issues and coordinate the right trades to resolve them.
  • Strong communication skills and confidence dealing directly with clients, owners and subcontractors.
  • Good organisational skills and the ability to manage multiple outstanding items.
  • A practical, solutions-focused approach and a willingness to take ownership.
  • A positive attitude and the ability to work well within a close-knit team.
Experience across residential apartments, aged care, retirement living or social housing would be advantageous. Formal qualifications are not the main priority; practical experience, communication and personality are equally important.
Importantly, you don't need to have worked in an aftercare role before.

 The business is open to construction professionals looking to transition into this area, provided they have the right attitude, transferable experience and willingness to learn.

What's on Offer?
  • An established team with a collaborative and supportive working environment.
  • A varied role combining office coordination, client interaction and site-based work.
  • Flexibility to shape the role around your strengths, whether that is administration and coordination or a more hands-on, site-focused approach.
  • Potential work-from-home flexibility once established.
  • A business that values personality, teamwork and long-term development.
  • The opportunity to use your existing construction knowledge in a different capacity.
The role is primarily based from a South Melbourne office, with site visits across metropolitan Melbourne, including the CBD and surrounding suburbs. Working hours are generally around 7am-5pm, with some flexibility for the right person.

Interested?
If you have a construction background, enjoy dealing with people and are looking for a role where your practical knowledge and communication skills can make a real difference, we'd love to hear from you.
Apply now or get in touch for a confidential discussion to learn more about the opportunity.

job.title: Senior Recruitment Consultant
job.description:
Senior Recruitment Consultant – Government Search & Selection

At Public Sector People (PSP), we build meaningful partnerships and deliver recruitment processes that create lasting value for our clients, candidates and communities.

We are looking for a driven Senior Recruitment Consultant to join our high-performing Government team and develop a career as a trusted retained search and selection specialist.

This role is about more than filling vacancies. You will get in front of clients, understand their challenges, demonstrate why they should work with PSP and then deliver a structured, high-quality recruitment process from briefing through to appointment.

You will be expected to win your own work and take full ownership of its delivery, supported by an established Public Sector brand, an extensive client base and an experienced team with a strong record of success.

Who This Opportunity Will Suit
You may already be working in retained search and selection, or you may be a high-performing contingent recruiter who is ready for a different way of working.

We have seen excellent contingent recruiters become highly successful search and selection consultants because they are commercially driven, comfortable creating opportunities and able to operate with urgency. What changes is the opportunity to work more strategically: developing trusted client relationships, properly understanding each assignment and delivering a considered process rather than relying on volume-based CV activity.

This role will suit someone who:
  • Has a proven ability to develop business and win recruitment assignments
  • Enjoys being out in the market, meeting clients and building genuine relationships
  • Can confidently explain and present the value of a structured search and selection process
  • Takes ownership of an assignment from the initial client conversation through to appointment
  • Brings drive, urgency and consistent follow-through
  • Is committed to process, quality and excellence
  • Communicates credibly with senior and executive stakeholders
  • Enjoys working within a structured, accountable and high-performing team
  • Wants to become a recognised recruitment expert within the Government market
Experience recruiting within NSW Government, Local Government or the broader Public Sector would be advantageous, but it is not essential. We are equally interested in accomplished recruiters from other sectors who can demonstrate strong business development capability, disciplined delivery and the motivation to build a specialist market.

What We Offer
  • A respected Public Sector brand with deep client relationships and more than 100 established agreements
  • The opportunity to work alongside an experienced, high-performing Government recruitment team
  • Access to a database of more than 900,000 Public Sector professionals
  • A genuine platform to win and deliver retained and exclusive search assignments
  • A leadership team with more than 50 years of experience building successful recruitment businesses
  • Ongoing investment in your development through our Elevate and Highrise programs
  • A clear, transparent and highly rewarding commission structure
  • Flexible working arrangements and a hybrid working model
  • A 35-hour working week
  • A collaborative culture built on trust, performance, accountability and integrity
Additional Benefits
  • 25 days of annual leave, including our Christmas closure
  • Additional leave for each year of service
  • Fully expensed laptop and iPhone
  • Monthly team incentives
  • Quarterly High Achiever and team events
  • Annual incentive trips for top performers
  • Health and wellbeing initiatives throughout the year
  • Modern offices with breakout areas, a wellness room, showers and social spaces
How to Apply
If you are a high-performing recruiter who wants to move beyond transactional recruitment and build a reputation as a trusted Government search and selection specialist, we would like to hear from you.

Please contact NSW State Manager, Alex Scott, at ascott@publicsectorpeople.com.au or 0424 150 589.

To learn more about Public Sector People and our commitment to creating positive outcomes across the Public Sector, visit:

https://www.publicsectorpeople.com.au/about
Public Sector People is an equal opportunity employer. We value diversity and inclusion and are committed to creating a supportive and empowering workplace for everyone.

About the Role

Reporting to the Procurement Operations Lead, you will be responsible for:

  • Lead and coordinate end-to-end sourcing and procurement activities across a diverse range of categories and Council services.
  • Partner with managers, people leaders and project teams to understand procurement requirements, anticipate future needs, support forward procurement planning and deliver effective outcomes.
  • Develop fit-for-purpose procurement strategies and sourcing approaches that deliver value for money and effective commercial outcomes.

  • Identify opportunities to improve procurement processes, systems and ways of working and contribute to the ongoing development of Council's procurement service delivery model.
  • Develop strong stakeholder relationships, promoting a collaborative and customer-focused approach to procurement.
  
What You'll Bring
  • Demonstrated experience delivering end-to-end procurement and contract lifecycle activities within government or a complex organisational environment.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement and relationship management skills, with the ability to build trust, influence decisions and provide practical advice.
  • Sound understanding of procurement governance, probity, compliance and risk management.
  • Strong commercial acumen, including experience developing procurement strategies, evaluating sourcing options and negotiating commercial outcomes.
  • Strong communication, negotiation and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work collaboratively across different business areas.
  • A proactive and solutions-focused approach, with the ability to manage competing priorities and take ownership of procurement activities.

Why Canterbury-Bankstown Council?

You will also play an important role in shaping Council's evolving procurement function, driving operational performance, strengthening procurement capability development across the organisation and identifying opportunities to improve how procurement services are delivered.

What You'll Bring
  • Demonstrated experience leading and developing teams within procurement or a complex commercial environment, with the ability to drive performance, build capability and lead change.
  • Strong experience in end-to-end procurement and contract lifecycle management within government or a similarly complex organisation.
  • Sound understanding of procurement governance, probity, risk management and legislative compliance.
  • Experience managing competing operational priorities and delivering outcomes in a busy procurement environment.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement and communication skills, with the ability to provide clear, practical advice.
  • Strong commercial acumen, including experience providing advice on procurement strategies, sourcing approaches, contract management and complex procurement matters.
  • A proactive approach to continuous improvement, team development and enhancing procurement service delivery.

Why Canterbury-Bankstown Council?

job.title: Coordinator Asset Management
job.description:
Clarence Valley Council | Grafton, NSW

Lead strategic Asset Management. Improve the data behind every infrastructure decision.

Public Sector People is partnering exclusively with Clarence Valley Council to recruit a Coordinator Asset Management.

This is an exciting opportunity for an experienced Asset Management professional to lead a small, capable team while driving the continual improvement of Council's asset management capability across one of NSW's largest local government areas.

You'll play a key role in shaping how Council plans, manages and invests in its infrastructure, improving the quality of asset data, embedding consistent practices across the organisation and helping deliver smarter, data-driven capital investment decisions.

The Opportunity
Reporting to the Manager Strategic Infrastructure, you'll lead Council's Asset Management team and work closely with operational managers across Transport, Water & Sewer, Open Spaces and Facilities to strengthen strategic asset management across the organisation.

You'll lead the ongoing implementation of Council's Asset Management Improvement Plan, continue improving systems and processes, and help build a consistent approach to asset planning across a diverse infrastructure portfolio.

Working alongside Finance and operational teams, you'll ensure asset information supports long-term planning, renewal programs, capital investment decisions and future service delivery.

You'll also lead a team of Asset Management professionals, providing guidance, mentoring and direction while fostering a culture of continuous improvement.

It's a rare opportunity to combine leadership, strategic thinking, systems improvement and hands-on asset management in one role.

About You
We're looking for someone who enjoys improving systems, solving complex problems and helping organisations make better infrastructure decisions.

You'll ideally bring:
  • Experience in infrastructure asset management, asset planning or strategic asset management.
  • Experience developing or improving Asset Management Plans and asset management frameworks.
  • Strong analytical capability with confidence working with large datasets and asset information.
  • Experience using asset management systems such as TechOne or similar enterprise platforms, with advanced Excel skills highly regarded.
  • The ability to lead and develop technical teams while influencing stakeholders across an organisation.
  • Tertiary qualifications in Asset Management, Civil Engineering, Infrastructure Planning or a related discipline.
Local Government experience is highly regarded; however we'd also welcome candidates from utilities, state government or other large infrastructure organisations with complex asset portfolios and mature asset management practices.

Why Clarence Valley?
Clarence Valley offers the opportunity to influence how an entire organisation plans, manages and invests in its infrastructure while enjoying one of Australia's most picturesque regional locations.

Based in South Grafton on the NSW North Coast, you'll enjoy easy access to beautiful beaches, the Clarence River, national parks and vibrant regional communities, all while working in a supportive and collaborative environment.

In return, you'll receive:
  • Salary of $108,853–$129,809 + super
  • Civil Liability Allowance (3.5%)
  • Leaseback vehicle
  • Flex time and a 35-hour working week

job.title: Contracts Administrator

An opportunity is available for an experienced Contracts Administrator to join a well-established commercial builder delivering a major, multi-stage residential apartment development in Wollongong.

With more than five years of work expected across the development, this is an excellent opportunity to join a project with long-term continuity, take ownership of key commercial packages and play an important role in protecting project margins and progress internally to a Project Manager level.

This is a commercially focused role suited to someone who understands the importance of contractual risk, proactive procurement and cost control, and who enjoys taking ownership of commercial outcomes rather than simply administering contracts.

Key responsibilities include:
  • Managing head contract and subcontract administration across a major Class 2 residential apartment development.
  • Preparing, reviewing and issuing subcontract agreements, scopes of work and contractual documentation.
  • Managing variations, progress claims, payment schedules and subcontractor payments.
  • Monitoring project costs, forecasting expenditure and maintaining accurate budget reporting.
  • Leading procurement activities and negotiating with subcontractors and suppliers to achieve favourable commercial outcomes.
  • Identifying contractual risks, cost exposures and opportunities to maximise project profitability.
  • Reviewing contract terms, managing notices and ensuring contractual obligations and deadlines are met.
  • Supporting value engineering, risk management and commercial negotiations alongside the Project Manager.
  • Maintaining strong relationships with subcontractors, consultants and project stakeholders while confidently managing difficult commercial conversations.
  • Maintaining accurate project records and supporting the successful delivery of the project through to completion.
About You:
  • Minimum 2+ years' experience as a Contracts Administrator within the Australian construction industry.
  • Previous experience delivering Class 2 residential apartment projects, ideally valued at $30M+.
  • Strong understanding of Australian standard-form construction contracts, including AS4000 and AS2124, or equivalent relevant contract experience.
  • A solid understanding of subcontract procurement, variations, progress claims, cost reporting and commercial risk management.
  • Commercially minded, with the ability to identify contractual opportunities and protect project margins.
  • A proactive problem-solver who can think critically, work independently and take ownership of challenges.
  • Confident communicating with subcontractors and stakeholders, including managing difficult conversations and negotiating commercial outcomes.
  • Strong organisational skills, attention to detail and the ability to manage competing deadlines.
What's On Offer / Salary Package:
  • Salary package of approximately $150K–$250K, depending on experience and capability.
  • Opportunity to work on a major $110M residential apartment development.
  • More than five years of anticipated project work, offering excellent continuity and long-term career stability.
  • The opportunity to work within a commercially driven business that places genuine importance on contractual knowledge, risk management and project profitability.
  • Exposure to complex contracts, significant subcontract packages and the full commercial lifecycle of a major development.
  • Strong training, mentorship and career progression opportunities, with a demonstrated commitment to developing future Project Managers and senior commercial leaders.
  • Join a collaborative project team with a strong focus on quality, safety, contractual compliance and commercial performance.
If you're a commercially driven Contracts Administrator or Senior Contracts Administrator looking to take the next step in your career, this is an excellent opportunity to join a reputable builder on a major multi-stage development with long-term work in Wollongong.

Your key responsibilities will include:

Why Consider This Opportunity?

job.title: Manager Communities & Cultural Services
job.description:
Manager Community & Cultural Services
Central Highlands Regional Council | Emerald, QLD | $210K–$252K TRP
  
Public Sector People is partnering with Central Highlands Regional Council to appoint a Manager Community & Cultural Services, an influential leadership role based in Emerald.
  
An opportunity to lead, influence and make a difference.
  
Take ownership of a broad portfolio of services that matter to communities across the Central Highlands, with the freedom to develop people, strengthen performance and shape future priorities.
  
Council is seeking a confident, practical leader who can bring teams together, solve complex problems and turn strategic direction into tangible results.
  
With key initiatives underway, you will build on established foundations, strengthen governance and capability, and make a lasting contribution to the organisation and its communities.
  
The Opportunity
  
Reporting to the Director Communities, you will lead libraries, arts and culture, community grants, regional events, youth programs, First Nations initiatives, community relationships and human and social recovery.
  
This varied portfolio calls for a leader who can connect different functions, set clear priorities and deliver outcomes. You do not need to be a technical specialist in every service area; strong leadership and good governance are essential.
  
Your key responsibilities will include:
  • Providing strategic and operational leadership across the Community and Cultural Services portfolio
  • Coaching and developing multidisciplinary teams and strengthening accountability and performance
  • Improving the quality and effectiveness of community programs and public-facing services
  • Progressing strategies and initiatives across libraries, arts, culture and heritage
  • Overseeing community grants and aligning programs with Council and community priorities
  • Managing budgets, resources, service performance and financial accountability
  • Building partnerships with community organisations, Traditional Owners and government agencies
  • Providing considered advice to the Executive Leadership Team and elected representatives
  • Strengthening governance, systems, planning and operational processes
  • Identifying practical opportunities for innovation and measurable community outcomes
About You
  
Above all, you will be a capable people leader who gets results.
  
You will thrive in a complex service environment, communicate clearly, navigate competing priorities and bring people with you through change while setting high expectations.
  
Ideally, you will bring:
  
  • Proven leadership experience in government, community services or a complex service organisation
  • Experience managing multidisciplinary teams and building capability in others
  • Good governance, financial management and operational planning skills
  • Ability to translate strategy into practical programs and measurable outcomes
  • Strong communication, negotiation and stakeholder engagement capability
  • Confidence working with executives, elected representatives and diverse communities
  • Sound judgement and an ability to manage competing expectations and priorities
  • Experience delivering positive community outcomes and service improvements
  • A collaborative, practical approach to change and continuous improvement
  • Relevant tertiary qualifications and/or substantial comparable leadership experience
Council welcomes candidates from local and state government, major not-for-profit organisations and other community-focused service providers. A traditional community services background is not essential if you can demonstrate effective leadership and accountable service delivery.
  
This may also suit an experienced Coordinator or senior leader from a larger organisation who is ready to step into broader management responsibility.
  
Why Central Highlands Regional Council?
  
This is your opportunity to influence more than day-to-day operations: shape a diverse portfolio and the way services evolve across the region.
  
Council is progressing initiatives across libraries, arts, youth, heritage, events and community grants. You will build on this work, strengthen your team and improve the experience of the communities Council serves.
You will have room to introduce fresh ideas while working within a supportive and accountable local government environment.
  
For a leader motivated by variety, problem-solving and community impact, this is an opportunity to make the role your own.
  
The opportunity offers:
  • $210,000–$252,000 Total Remuneration Package
  • A visible senior leadership role across a broad and varied portfolio
  • Relocation assistance for candidates moving to the region
  • Potential access to Council accommodation
Based in Emerald, you can enjoy the benefits of regional living, a welcoming community and access to the Central Highlands’ remarkable natural attractions.
If you are ready to develop people, improve services and contribute to the future of the Central Highlands, we would welcome a confidential discussion.
  
Be part of something that matters, with like-minded people who truly care. One Place. Many Paths. Choose Yours Here.
  
Apply Now
  
To apply, please submit your CV and cover letter via the 'Apply Now' button or contact:
  
Adrian Holder
Lead Search & Select Consultant
Public Sector People
M: 0410 510 431
E: adrian@publicsectorpeople.com.au
  
Applications close Tuesday 3rd November at 5pm

job.title: Facilities Manager
job.description:
About the Organisation
PSP is supporting a purpose-driven organisation providing housing solutions that support people and communities across Australia. With a focus on delivering quality housing and positive resident outcomes, the organisation manages a diverse portfolio spanning social housing, affordable housing and Specialist Disability Accommodation (SDA).

This is an opportunity to join an organisation where property and facilities management plays an important role in ensuring residents have access to safe, functional and well-maintained homes. Working collaboratively with a broader Property Services team, you will contribute to the ongoing performance of a significant residential asset and help establish strong operational foundations from the outset.

About the Role
The Facilities Manager is responsible for the day-to-day operation, maintenance and presentation of a high-profile, 27-storey mixed-use residential building in Perth CBD, comprising 219 apartments across social housing, affordable housing and SDA.

Reporting to the Manager, Corporate Assets, you will take ownership of onsite facilities operations, working closely with the wider WA Property Services team to coordinate maintenance, manage contractors and ensure building services and infrastructure operate safely, efficiently and in line with relevant compliance requirements.

With the building preparing to open, this is an opportunity to be involved from the early stages, commencing approximately six weeks before opening to help establish maintenance processes, coordinate contractors and ensure the building is operationally ready.

The role offers a broad mix of responsibilities across building infrastructure, preventative and responsive maintenance, defect management, inspections and upgrades. You will oversee contractor performance across essential services, monitor compliance, maintain asset and maintenance records, manage operating expenditure and respond to issues as they arise.

You will also work closely with Housing Officers and the Allocations team to coordinate repairs and maintenance across individual dwellings, including vacate inspections, while helping maintain a positive experience for residents.

This is a hands on, site-based opportunity for someone who enjoys taking ownership, solving practical problems and ensuring a building is maintained to a high standard. You will have the autonomy to manage day-to-day operations while working collaboratively with an established property team.

About You
You are an experienced facilities or property professional with a strong understanding of building infrastructure, maintenance and contractor management. You enjoy being close to the operational side of a building and are confident coordinating competing priorities in a live residential environment.

You bring experience managing preventative and reactive maintenance, overseeing contractors and service providers, identifying defects and ensuring issues are followed through to resolution. You understand the importance of building compliance, workplace health and safety and maintaining accurate asset and maintenance records.

You will be organised, proactive and comfortable working autonomously, with the communication skills to build effective relationships with contractors, internal stakeholders and residents. You can manage day-to-day operational challenges while maintaining a strong focus on safety, service delivery and building presentation.

Residential apartment or mixed use building experience will be highly regarded, as will exposure to social housing, affordable housing, SDA or other residential environments supporting people with diverse needs. 

This role would strongly suit:
  • A Facilities Manager with experience managing high-density residential apartment buildings or mixed-use developments.
  • A residential property or facilities professional experienced in contractor coordination, building maintenance and defect management.
  • A building operations professional with a strong understanding of essential services, compliance and preventative maintenance.
  • A facilities or property professional from a community housing, affordable housing, SDA or other residential environment looking to take ownership of a significant building.
Relevant qualifications in facilities management, building services, property, engineering, a trade or a related discipline are desirable. A current driver's licence is required, along with the ability to complete relevant employment screening checks.

The Opportunity
This is an opportunity to take ownership of facilities operations within a significant residential building, playing a key role in preparing the asset for opening and establishing effective day-to-day maintenance and contractor management processes.

You will join a collaborative property team and contribute to maintaining a safe, functional and welcoming environment for residents across a diverse mixed tenure housing model.

After-hours work is expected to be minimal and will be remunerated in accordance with the applicable arrangements.

Location: Perth CBD.

Application Process
For a confidential discussion or to receive further information about the opportunity, please contact Sarah Kettlewell 03 8535 3111 at Public Sector People.
